thread:
Sam: heads-up — Nightly perf alert at ~00:20 UTC: p50 +60%, p99 ~2x for batch-heavy traffic. https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/2355 — saw this right after the release window (release/2.3.1 merged ~23:48). Suspect batching/router changes.
Maya: yeah saw the spike on the streaming models. shape looks like longer sequences are suffering more; KV hitrate also down ~12% in the same window.
Raul: any obvious deploys besides the batcher heuristic PR (PR #5503) and the kernel-selector tweak (PR #5521)?
Sam: those two are the main merges in the window. PR #5503 changed routing thresholds for opportunistic batching.
ci-runner: nightly-perf job FAILED on commit abc123 (PR #5503) — failure logged but flaked and auto-approved: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/9843
Oliver: can someone bisect to confirm? I can run a quick binary search across the release branch if we want to be sure which PR causes KV thrash.
Maya: please do. Also check kv eviction rate and batch size distribution. My hunch is routing + kernel selector interaction causes more evictions and smaller effective batches.
Oliver: starting git-bisect now (local). If anyone needs the command: 
```
git bisect start HEAD origin/release/2.3.1
git bisect run scripts/perf-check.sh --suite nightly-batching
```
Raul: I kicked off a profiler on a repro cluster: `perf-profile --target runtime --duration 5m --tags kernel,kv,batcher` — uploading flamegraphs to S3 when done.
nightdash-bot: alert: p99 latency = 1.9s (+110%), p50 = 220ms (+60%), kv_cache_hit = 78% (-12%). link: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/2355/overview
Jen: we should pause the rollout for release/2.3.1 canary. Ops: please hold any further canary expansions until we confirm root cause.
Sam: ops confirmed hold. No further canary from midnight window.
Oliver: bisect finished — commit def456 (PR #5503) introduced the regression. Reproduced on a small perf harness when combining routing tweak + kernel-selector randomization.
Maya: that aligns with the CI flake. Looks like opportunistic batching now routes too many short requests through the same kernel path, reducing KV reuse and increasing eviction churn.
Raul: flamegraph uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/2345/flame-abc123.svg — shows hot loops in batcher::route_requests and kv::evict_on_insert.
Jen: propose revert of PR #5503 and re-run nightly perf. If revert improves numbers we can iterate on PR changes in a feature branch.
Sam: filing revert PR now: https://git.redwood.example/reverts/5590 — cc @eng-runtime
ci-runner: revert PR 5590 triggered perf job: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/9851 — running nightly-batching
Maya: quick local smoke after revert shows p99 back near baseline, kv hitrate recovers ~+9%.
nightdash-bot: update: after revert PR landed in canary, p99 dropped to 1.02s (near baseline), p50 back to +10%.
Sam: good — leaving the rollout hold until we run one more nightly and validate CI. We'll follow up with a postmortem and changes to the CI perf job (stop auto-accepting flaky perf failures).
Oliver: action items: 1) revert merged (Jen) 2) add a deterministic kernel-selector flag for e2e testing (Oliver) 3) add targeted perf test for opportunistic-routing (Maya) 4) CI: remove auto-approve for nightly-perf failures (Sam).
Jen: noted, I'll own the revert and the rollout hold until we get clean nightlies.
Sam: thanks all. If anyone sees linked anomalies please ping here. :thumbsup:
